summary.headline: Sai Parenterals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 182 crore, EBITDA margin 14.9%; IPO funds Rs 101.85 crore redeployed to a 60% stake in Saicriti.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs 182 crore against Rs 201 crore in Q4 FY26, with gross margin up 370 bps QoQ to 41.8% and EBITDA of Rs 27 crore (14.9% margin). PAT was Rs 8 crore (4.3% margin), down from Rs 13.2 crore in Q4 on a normalised tax charge and lower revenue. The Board approved varying IPO objects, moving Rs 83.83 crore from Jeedimetla upgrades to a 60% stake in Saicriti Pharma and Rs 18.02 crore from a greenfield R&D centre to a 60% stake in Prathyak Laboratories (Rs 15 crore), both subject to shareholder approval. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of Rs 750 crore revenue at about 17% EBITDA margin, weighted to H2.

segments.name: Noumed Pharmaceuticals (Australia/NZ)
segments.commentary: Consolidated since 12 Nov 2025; Q1 revenue was hit by West Asia shipping delays, forcing air freight and extra regulatory costs. Renewed EBOS (TerryWhite Chemmart, Pharmacy Choice) OTC contract from 1 July 2026, valued at AUD 202 million (about Rs 1,300 crore) over 7.5 years, roughly AUD 27 million a year.

segments.name: Standalone (India, injectables and exports)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue Rs 56 crore with EBITDA margin about 29%, attributed mainly to operating leverage. Current exports are only oral dosage and cephalosporins; domestic injectables dominate Units 1 and 2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reiterated: revenue Rs 750 crore and EBITDA margin about 17%, with a 45:55 H1:H2 split (CFO-era statement also referred to 44:55 in Q&A).
Q1 revenue is said to be about 24% of the full-year Rs 750 crore target, ahead of the phasing needed.
Noumed Australia contribution from the EBOS renewal begins in Q2 FY27.
Management expects the recovery of raw material cost increases to flow through the contract book over Q2 as the 90-120 day price-revision lag unwinds.
FY27 described as a building year; FY28 expected to show the impact. No FY28 number given; management will decide at Q3 call.
Management expects peak debt in FY27 with de-leveraging from FY28.
capex_capacity: Saicriti Pharma (60% stake, Rs 83.83 crore, total project cost about Rs 215-217 crore): critical care injectable facility at Gummadidala, outside the outer ring road, over 15,000 sq yd; completion extended to about April 2027; about 154.66 million units of capacity vs about 105 million under the original Jeedimetla upgrade (about 47% more).
Jeedimetla Units 1 and 2 (about 3,100 sq yd) cannot be expanded and fall within the outer ring road, where upgrades are no longer permitted under HILTP policy.
Prathyak Laboratories (60%, Rs 15 crore): R&D centre at Genome Valley, Hyderabad, expected to complete on or before 30 September 2026; to be renamed Sai Prathyak as a step-down subsidiary.

Australia (Noumed) facility: AUD 53 million total programme funding now complete; physical completion targeted January 2027, TGA inspection by March 2027, Phase 1 manufacturing from April 2027. Packing-line validation through December-February.

Local manufacture is expected to cut Noumed inventory from 9-10 months to about 5-6 months of stock; one Indian container of inputs replaces 8 finished-goods containers. Federal Modern Manufacturing Initiative grant of AUD 20 million cited.
demand_pricing: Noumed holds 5 exclusive long-term contracts and 10 exclusive supply molecule contracts covering 526 SKUs, typically 5+ years.
Wesfarmers Health and EBOS networks together cover over 2,900 of about 5,500 Australian pharmacies.

EBOS contract: about 12 new products per year targeted; first 24 NPD products identified, with 8 to be developed by Sai's R&D (6 started), 4 exclusive supply contracts and the rest via a Catalent soft-gel partnership.
Management said pharmacy-channel growth for some molecules is running at about 8%, and that more order wins of similar size should come over the next year.
Prathyak pipeline: 150 SKUs across 86 molecules (lyophilised, liposomal, nano-based, oncology and critical-care injectables).
Management stated the injectables export plan targets Europe, Southeast Asia, Latin America and the Middle East first, with the US to be reviewed later.
Saicriti existing domestic critical care franchise about Rs 52-53 crore, currently produced via CMOs and to move to the new site.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 12 new NPD products included in the AUD 202 million EBOS order value, and should more order wins of similar size be expected over the next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Mark Thulborne said the NPD products sit on top of the order value, which reflects the existing supply portfolio. He said more order wins of this size should come over the next year, with pharmacy-network growth of about 5-8% a year.

qa_highlights.question: Given the many parallel initiatives (Noumed integration, capacity, R&D, US entry), how is management bandwidth protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Anil K K said Sai is retaining the existing Noumed management, which holds 25.4% of Noumed, and the 4 senior Prathyak managers, with Sai providing manufacturing, funding and procurement support.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire 60% of a new facility rather than upgrade Jeedimetla as originally planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a Telangana government order that red and orange category units must move out of the outer ring road, which blocked upgrades at Units 1 and 2. Jeedimetla is about 3,100 sq yd against the 12,000-13,000 sq yd an EU-GMP plant needs, and a greenfield start would take 6-8 months just for land and approvals.

qa_highlights.question: What incremental products and markets will the new facility unlock, and why is there a pricing decline in injectables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first targets are Europe, Southeast Asia, Latin America and the Middle East, with the US to be reviewed later. Historically Units 1 and 2 served domestic injectables only, while exports were limited to oral dosage and cephalosporins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saicriti shareholding and the related-party status, and what are the funding details?
qa_highlights.answer: Saicriti is not a related party, per management. Critigen Pharma, with its subsidiary Questus Pharma, holds the remaining 40%, around Rs 56 crore, with the balance funded through project debt on a total project cost of about Rs 217 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 margin decline from Noumed a one-off, and is the guidance upgrade possible?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the Noumed cost hit was one-time, from West Asia supply constraints that drove extra freight and regulatory costs. Management reiterated Rs 750 crore revenue and about 17% EBITDA for FY27, declined to give an FY28 number, and will revisit at Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt trajectory and peak debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt was about Rs 310 crore at 30 June 2026 versus about Rs 320 crore in March 2026, after repaying about Rs 50 crore of loans from IPO proceeds. Management expects peak debt in FY27, with gross debt-to-equity around 0.6 times even at peak, and de-leveraging from FY28.

risks_watch: Execution on Saicriti: completion is extended to about April 2027 and the project depends on shareholder approval, project debt and the promoters' 40% contribution.
Noumed Australia: the Q2 gross margin recovery depends on raw material price pass-through (90-120 day lag) and the EBOS renewal starting in Q2 FY27.
Australian facility timelines: physical completion January 2027, TGA inspection by March 2027, Phase 1 manufacturing from April 2027.
FY27 H2 weighting: Rs 750 crore revenue needs a steep ramp after Q1 at about 24% of target; the H1:H2 split is quoted as both 45:55 and 44:55.
Debt peak in FY27 with new project debt added at subsidiary level, and the US subsidiary is at a preliminary evaluation stage with no tax or capex details.
Q1 PAT fell to Rs 8 crore from Rs 13.2 crore in Q4 on a normalised tax charge, and consolidated revenue declined QoQ.
key_quotes: I would emphasize that this improvement was achieved on a lower revenue base, and it was achieved despite absorbing elevated air freight cost in Australia.
The purpose for which the IPO funds were raised namely European GMP compliant injectable capacity for regulated markets and a dedicated research and development platform remains entirely unchanged.
FY '27 remains a year of building. FY '28 is when the build should start showing in our performance.
Now, it is too premature to discuss this part because now the US subsidiary whichever we are going to, which we took the permission from the board to start a US subsidiary.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic rationale and the Rs 750 crore / 17% FY27 guidance, but cautious on FY28 (no number given) and evasive on the US entry, which management called premature. Several answers were hedged or muddled, including the H1:H2 split and the debt-to-equity figure.
